items.title: Adrian Cunningham interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 31, 2021
items.q: I’m a big Brecker fan so you’d hang out at Seventh Avenue South and see Jaco playing

ctx.x: If you could get in a time machine and go to a specific, oh I’ll say a musical event, a recording event, is there something that you would just really like to be at and witness?

Wow. You know I think being not particularly specific but I’d love to have seen New York in the 70s, I’d love to have been here when there was just so much happening, you know when you had, well I’m a big Brecker fan so you’d hang out at Seventh Avenue South and see Jaco playing and all those geniuses and just seeing that, it just seemed like New York had such an incredible cultural life. It was probably, the city must have been so shitty in the seventies. You must have been — were you old enough to go out in the…

Oh yes. But I didn’t, not in New York. But yes, New York, from my recollection did have rough years during that decade as far as how the city was doing. But I find it interesting that you say that because maybe older musicians might say yeah I’d love to go to New York but they might have said during the 52nd Street heyday. So I think it’s very interesting that you say the seventies.
